final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and explicitly relied on the same record while narrowing the claim. That narrowing is valid as characterization: the issue is a specific disclosure/materiality dispute rather than a general launch-readiness failure. But that reinterpretation does not close the compliance gap identified in the initial report. The controlling policy requires a material limitation affecting a named launch use case or contractual customer segment to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows a named segment gap, two paid pilot commitments, an open legal ticket, and no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. That makes this more than a caveat about wording or monitoring posture; the caveat itself is an unresolved compliance predicate. Because no genuinely new admissible evidence closed any initial concern, a move to compliant_with_caveats is not supported.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which keeps the weakness material under the stated policy text.
The release policy still requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence of resolution, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap.
Legal review is still open, so the policy predicate governing disclosure/materiality remains unresolved on the record.
Aggregate readiness passing and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents still do not satisfy the separate disclosure/materiality requirement.
Generic NIST-style risk-management guidance and general model-card guidance still do not override or satisfy the specific internal release policy.
